spaceobject.annaherman.desc:
A small Main Belt asteroid nicknamed the Singing Rock for the strange acoustic phenomena heard within its caverns. These sounds, a combination of humming and groaning, similar to the human voice, have repeatedly forced miners to abandon their posts. The four mining settlements on Annagerman are currently not owned by any major corporations. Operations are always conducted through temporary proxies. Nobody wants to end up in the news for being held responsible for the mysterious disappearance of another mining group. However, rumors of rare lithium deposits continue to attract desperate loners and small teams of prospectors who, to protect themselves, are always linked with major players in the anarcho-capitalist system through a series of intermediaries.

Deep within the asteroid, there is a network of natural tunnels where strange signs are sometimes found, as if left by intelligent beings.The official stance is that these signs are hallucinations caused by oxygen system malfunctions in the suits of those who discovered them.
spaceobject.annaherman.name: Annagerman
spaceobject.annaherman.shortdesc:
A mining asteroid with incredibly difficult living and working conditions.
Beginning of development: first half of the 22nd century.
Main contribution to development: independent prospector groups.
spaceobject.callisto.desc:
Callisto has earned the status of a second Venus in miniature, as terraforming has made its atmosphere breathable, although not ideal. A mild climate with cool winds, coniferous and bush GMO vegetation and fields reminiscent of the northern steppes—all this makes Callisto a cozy oasis among the harsh conditions of the rest of Jupiter’s satellites. The soil is enriched with carbon dioxide, and the artificial ecosystem is gradually evolving, allowing grain and individual vegetable crops to be grown in the open.

The local settlers are very relaxed. However, it was on Callisto that an entire army of corporate resource hunters landed, assuming that many useful minerals were still to be found under the surface. In addition, the satellite has become a stopover for long-haul flights—sometimes secret equipment is hidden here. A forest of eternal night and cold.
spaceobject.callisto.name: Callisto
spaceobject.callisto.shortdesc:
Terraformed moon of Jupiter.
A joint project of Fresco and Tianming.
Tundra steppes and coniferous forests under a thin but breathable atmosphere.
spaceobject.ceres.desc:
The largest asteroid in the Main Belt. Settlements on Ceres appeared even before the Great Anarchist Revolution (GAR). The asteroid is not only rich in valuable ores, but also serves as a launchpad for mining expeditions throughout the Main Belt. Epitoma Colony and theEos station compete for the title of capital of Ceres. Both are home to offices and other buildings belonging to corporations operating on the border of the Outer and Inner Systems. Many stations are located inside the asteroid, while several inhabited settlements revolve around it.

Also not far from Ceres is the artificial planet Wernher, which moves at a synchronized speed.
spaceobject.ceres.name: Ceres
spaceobject.ceres.shortdesc:
The largest asteroid of the Main Belt, a major trading port.
Start of development: 2070s.
Main contributors: Dilthey, Hive, PlanetBridge, CoreWard MG, with minor contributions from the old states of Earth.
spaceobject.citadel.desc:
Citadel-1 is an artificial satellite of Mercury. Tianming Corporation installed cubecentric engines on this trans-Neptunian object and launched it into Mercury's orbit. After the asteroid was delivered to its permanent location, a habitable ring was built around it along the minor axis. After that, Citadel-1 was spun at such speed that the Coriolis force was able to serve as a substitute for gravity for people. Four of the five Citadel-1 stations are located in the habitable ring. However, the Gamma Hydra 4 station is located inside the asteroid itself. Tianming was a pioneer in asteroid capture.

Citadel-1 is an old complex and lacks the amenities found on HAVOC or Geist.
spaceobject.citadel.name: Citadel-1
spaceobject.citadel.shortdesc:
An artificial satellite of Mercury, made from a captured asteroid.
Altitude above Mercury: 350 Mm.
Year of creation: 2102
Creator: Tianming.
spaceobject.deimos.desc:
Mars is a backwater relative to Earth. Phobos and Deimos are backwaters relative to Mars. Deimos is a natural satellite of Mars, a shadow port on the edge of the Inner System. Here you can meet not only pirates and other public enemies, but also corporate agents who want to infiltrate the factions of the Outer System. Deimos is not just a "forge of evil". Here, hidden from the eyes of corporations, new independent ideas are born.

Deimos is like a spider waiting for its prey: quiet, inconspicuous, dangerous. Its venom is quite capable of harming the Inner System in the future.
spaceobject.deimos.name: Deimos
spaceobject.deimos.shortdesc:
A natural satellite of Mars, a shadow port on the border of the Inner System.
Start of exploration: 2050s.
Main contributors to development: RealWare, PlanetBridge.
Security status: not entirely safe.
spaceobject.earth.desc:
Earth is an ecological and agricultural paradise for humankind. According to SBN, the Earth is inhabited by four billion people. After the construction of Intercity on Mars and New Seattle on the Moon, the planet is under the Interdict Regulation. An information barrier has also been installed. All data is routed through ISS Station AES. Apparently, the SBN checks outgoing data from Earth. For this reason, not everyone believes the stories about paradise.

The Interdict Regulation: only employees of those corporations that own property here are allowed to visit Earth.
spaceobject.earth.name: Earth
spaceobject.earth.shortdesc:
The cradle of humanity, closed to the public.
Interdict regulation: active.
Ecological status: stable.
spaceobject.enceladus.desc:
Enceladus is a gleaming icy moon of Saturn. Here, geysers hurl plumes of water and ice hundreds of kilometers into space. These eruptions form a thin veil within Saturn’s rings and serve as a vital source of water. Beneath Enceladus’s frozen crust lies an ocean of liquid water, heated by tidal friction. Its depths remain largely unexplored, but it is precisely here that corporations dispatch submersible drones and research stations in the hope of discovering new forms of life.

Because of the constant eruptions, Enceladus’s surface is covered in fresh snow, making it one of the brightest bodies in the Solar System. As a result, there is only one permanent colony on the surface, while the other two settlements orbit above it.
spaceobject.enceladus.name: Enceladus
spaceobject.enceladus.shortdesc:
Icy moon of Saturn, covered in snow.
Colonization began: 2150s.
A key source of water in the Outer System.
spaceobject.europa.desc:
Europa, after partial but quite successful terraforming, is a white, snow-covered world hiding a giant ocean under a thick ice crust. Outwardly, the landscape resembles eternal polar deserts: Plateaus of ice, snow plains riddled with cracks. The internal ocean (thanks to the corporations, which launched geothermal heating programs) has become a source of unique flora and fauna, which mutates amazingly quickly under the influence of low temperatures and possible other factors.

Ground stations are connected by giant tunnels cut through the ice. Sometimes these ice corridors become overgrown with crystalline structures, and from time to time researchers encounter predatory microorganisms there. From the outside, it all looks like a set for a horror movie.

The Dilthey and Tianming corporations are actively researching the possibility of creating underwater bases for launching a submarine navigation system. However, there are complications due to the high risk of barotrauma.
spaceobject.europa.name: Europa
spaceobject.europa.shortdesc:
An icy planet with a warm subsurface ocean with unpredictable life.
Terraforming is limited, but allows for the creation of sustainable colonies.
spaceobject.fuller.desc:
An artificial satellite of the Moon. It rotates in a geostationary orbit and is constantly above Mare Imbrium. The satellite is named after Richard Buckminster Fuller—an outstanding architect, designer, engineer, inventor, philosopher, mathematician, writer, and poet. And, most importantly, a hopeless utopian whose ideas had no chance of becoming a reality under the oppression of states. The liberation granted to people by the Great Anarchist Revolution made it possible to implement many of Fuller's ideas. This artificial satellite of five station modules linked together by engineering structures is a genius's dream come true.

When the Sun rises over Mare Imbrium, Fuller reflects its light, as if speaking on behalf of humanity: "We are moving forward! We are building the future!"
spaceobject.fuller.name: Fuller
spaceobject.fuller.shortdesc:
An artificial satellite of the Moon, a space city complex.
Altitude above Moon: 400 Mm.
Year of creation: 2145.
Creators: Dilthey, Grasshopper Tek.
spaceobject.ganymede.desc:
Ganymede is not terraformed and resembles the Moon: gray dusty plains, sharp crater ridges and constant temperature changes. The atmosphere is preserved only in domes and subsurface colonies, but "gravitational compression" allows special equipment to work at fairly large distances. Mining is of paramount importance on Ganymede, but the infrastructure is much more modest than even in the Main Belt.

There are no vast mountain ranges suitable for shelter, but there are many scattered underground voids that are used to store equipment and set up remote secret bases.
spaceobject.ganymede.name: Ganymede
spaceobject.ganymede.shortdesc:
Largest satellite of Jupiter. A lifeless moon.
Under active exploration as of the early 2200s.
spaceobject.geist.desc:
Geist is a ghost asteroid. It was extremely difficult to detect due to its orbit, speed, albedo and other factors. However, the Dilthey corporation captured Geist and, using powerful cubecentric engines, altered its orbit so that the large asteroid became a transit point in the Main Belt. Beneath the surface of Geist are three colony stations. One of them even has a real city park. It is not only a transit point connecting the outer and inner parts of the System, but also a hub for legal activity in the Belt.

One of the stations is held by Dilthey. It became the headquarters of the corporation after the Wernher stations were transferred for free sale. The other two change hands depending on the fluctuations of the dignitas in the AnCap system.
spaceobject.geist.name: Geist
spaceobject.geist.shortdesc:
A captured asteroid, brought into the Main Belt; a space city complex.
Average distance to Sun: 3 AU
Year of creation: 2180.
Creator: Dilthey.
spaceobject.havoc.desc:
HAVOC — High Altitude Venusian Orbital City. This is an extremely successful project of the Dilthey Corporation. After being captured beyond the orbit of Neptune, the asteroid was delivered to the orbit of Venus. The asteroid served as a framework for an arcology — a city with a closed ecological system designed by the Italian philosopher and architect Paolo Soleri. The training station Blade at the Ready is located outside the arcology, under the surface of the asteroid.

All those lucky enough to live on HAVOC stations can enjoy the latest technologies in space dwelling design. Dilthey seems not to notice the shortage of resources and the growing tension, and lives in a real anarcho-capitalist paradise.
spaceobject.havoc.name: HAVOC
spaceobject.havoc.shortdesc:
An artificial satellite of Venus, made from a captured asteroid.
Altitude above Venus: 120 Mm.
Year of creation: 2192.
Creator: Dilthey.
spaceobject.hekate.desc: A small asteroid in the Main Belt that attracted the attention of the Civil Resistance due to its unremarkable nature. It was here that the colnodes delivered the quasimorph with whom they made the Alliance Pact.
spaceobject.hekate.name: Hecate
spaceobject.hekate.shortdesc: Main base of the Civil Resistance
spaceobject.hungary.desc:
The Belt’s bridgehead in the Inner System. 434 Hungaria and its asteroid group have orbits passing close to Mars. This makes it a key point for coordinating transit routes and mining expeditions to Mars and back to the Main Belt. Hungaria is known for its compact but strategically important settlements, each of which is surrounded by arrays of solar panels and antennas.

The largest settlement,Forward, serves as a transit hub and storage facility for expeditions. The asteroid’s surface features vast empty territories, which are used for testing new technologies and weapons. This attracts corporations seeking secure sites for testing hazardous innovations.

434 Hungaria straddles the border between two worlds: the Inner System and the Main Belt. For the Main Belt, it is considered relatively stable—until corporations instigate another reshuffling of power here.
spaceobject.hungary.name: 434 Hungaria
spaceobject.hungary.shortdesc:
An asteroid in the inner Main Belt. A transit base between the Belt and the Inner System. A weapons testing ground.
Beginning of development: late 2060s.
Major contribution to development: nation-states.
spaceobject.hygeia.desc:
Hygiea is infamous for its desolation and wretchedness. The asteroid is riddled with microcraters, resembling pores. In fact, its spongy structure holds numerous deposits of mineral salts.

Hygiea is almost completely devoid of large settlements, with the exception of the mining station Connelly-4, which is perpetually empty. Yet Hygiea is surprisingly densely populated. Small mining colonies, identified only by numbers, are scattered across its surface and hidden within the pores. This environment makes the asteroid a haven for various public enemies, the Civil Resistance, and other Belt inhabitants who remain invisible to the anarcho-capitalist system.

Local legends speak of “salt ghosts”—ethereal figures of glittering crystalline dust that emerge in the dark.
spaceobject.hygeia.name: Hygiea
spaceobject.hygeia.shortdesc:
An asteroid with colonies of various purposes.
Beginning of development: 2150s.
Main contribution to development: independent anonymous foundation.
spaceobject.hyperion.desc:
Hyperion is a chaotically rotating moon of Saturn and known for its sponge-like surface. Landing on Hyperion is a difficult task even for seasoned pilots. Its craters merge into complex systems of caves and tunnels. These labyrinths have become a separate challenge for specialized survey teams tasked with mapping them.

Because of its unpredictable rotation, building stable stations here is extremely difficult. Yet it is precisely this instability that draws corporations. The caves are ideal for concealing laboratories, clandestine manufacturing sites, and observation posts.
spaceobject.hyperion.name: Hyperion
spaceobject.hyperion.shortdesc:
A tunnel-riddled moon of Saturn with chaotic rotation.
Colonization began: 2180s.
Corporations develop Hyperion at their own risk.
spaceobject.interamnia.desc:
An aluminosilicate-rich Main Belt asteroid that was never destined to become a mining center. Unless you count the occasional desperate group of miners who, in a mad attempt to get rich, land in a random spot on Interamnia and try to collect as many stones as possible. The thing is, Interamnia is in eternal conflict. It is home to the largest and most open station owned by the enemies of society—space pirates. The city of Hargeisa is the Tortuga of the 23rd century.

Why hasn't RealWare nuked Interamnia yet? It is convenient for corporations to have a free zone where undercover agents can do business outside the AnCap system.
spaceobject.interamnia.name: Interamnia
spaceobject.interamnia.shortdesc:
A large asteroid of the Main Belt, a pirate base and a shadow port.
Start of development: unknown.
Main contributors to development: public enemies.
Security status: extremely unsafe.
spaceobject.io.desc:
Io is a glowing, volcanically active world, often referred to as the "burning planet." The surface is dotted with active volcanoes, sulfur geysers and lava lakes that glow at night. The atmosphere is thin, but partial terraforming by the Tianming Corporation has made it possible to briefly leave the bases without heavy equipment. However, a special spacesuit is still required. The gravity is weak, making it easy to navigate the rugged landscape, but treacherous volcanic ash falls make every step a risky challenge.

Some corporations are intensively mining the rare minerals that form around the volcanic zones. The planet itself continues to seethe, constantly changing its terrain.
spaceobject.io.name: Io
spaceobject.io.shortdesc:
A hyperactive world of lava and ash.
Terraforming has so far only reduced the extreme environment to manageable levels. It is a difficult place to live, but an invaluable source of rare resources.
spaceobject.jupiter.desc:
Jupiter is a gigantic colossus whose atmosphere is constantly disturbed by raging storms, giant tempests and continuous discharges of lightning hundreds of kilometers long. Terraforming of this quasi-star is, of course, impossible, but corporations are actively using the upper layers of the atmosphere to extract valuable gases and collect energy from colossal thunderstorms. Thanks to cubecentric engines, some tiny asteroids and modules have been transported to the upper layers of Jupiter and turned into floating stations. Some of these stations are surrounded by massive buffer rings capable of withstanding strong winds.

Jupiter’s powerful magnetic fields mean that all station communications must pass through special buffer nodes. Any failure to protect against radiation will lead to catastrophe: people working here often complain of dizzying visions, as if the planet's consciousness itself was trying to interact with them. These stories fuel rumors of strange mystical phenomena in the depths of Jupiter.
spaceobject.jupiter.name: Jupiter
spaceobject.jupiter.shortdesc:
Gas giant. Colonization is impossible.
Start of atmospheric exploration: various; active growth began in the 2150s, when corporations saw the benefit of cheap plasma and hydrogen resources.
spaceobject.mars.desc:
Mars was supposed to be terraformed before Venus, but the solar wind quickly blew away any atmosphere from Mars. All human efforts were reduced to maintaining the surface in the state of a cold desert with islands of GMO tundra closer to the equator. Acceptable oxygen levels and the ability to live without spacesuits still motivate people to explore Mars. Scattered across the surface are individual corporate bases, reminiscent of boomtowns from the Wild West. The only large city on the planet is Intercity.

It was built before the Great Anarchist Revolution (GAR). It was badly damaged and has not yet been fully restored. Intercity is a cold slum, with the occasional corporate buildings rising like beacons in an ocean of poverty.
spaceobject.mars.name: Mars
spaceobject.mars.shortdesc:
A terraformed planet covered with an unfriendly cold desert.
Start of exploration: 2040s.
Main contributions to terraforming: RealWare, CoreWard MG, and minor contributions from the old states of Earth.
spaceobject.mechta.desc:
At some point in the past, the USSR launched a tiny artificial planet called Mechta (Dream) toward the Sun. About 100 years ago, Venus attracted Mechta, and it became an artificial satellite of the planet. During the terraforming of Venus, Mechta became a convenient place for assembling structures and a loading terminal for planetary shuttles. Garbage was discarded next to Mechta, mechanisms were attached to it—and then they were forgotten about. As a result, Mechta became a huge improvised engineering art object and a surprise to everyone in the System.

Over time, Mechta became so large that stations began to be placed on it.
spaceobject.mechta.name: Mechta
spaceobject.mechta.shortdesc:
An artificial satellite of Venus made from space debris, which only grows in size every year.
Height above Venus: variable.
Year of creation: 1959, launch of the Luna-1 station.
Creator: USSR and various corporations.
spaceobject.mercury.desc:
In the 2150s, terraforming equipment was delivered to Mercury. Surprisingly quickly, it was possible to saturate the atmosphere with oxygen and nitrogen, and remove toxic gases. However, life on the surface of Mercury is impossible, and nobody was expecting it. Automatic stations operate on the surface.

But nonetheless, people are present on the planet. Inside mountain ranges and deep enough underground, it was possible to create underground colonies, isolated from the temperature conditions of the surface.
spaceobject.mercury.name: Mercury
spaceobject.mercury.shortdesc:
A planet with conditions sufficient for life underground.
Start of exploration: 2110s.
Main contributors to terraforming: none, the planet terraforms naturally.
